description:
## Why this ticket exists

D4 is one of the four prototype gates the plan treats as RELEASE gates, all scheduled **day-1 of their phase** so a failure re-plans early (Top risks #6). It is the only gate that is also an **OWNER DECISION with money attached**: Apple Developer ID membership, $99/yr — "Owner confirm pending (cost + Apple account)". Round-2 review sharpened the question: **notarization tickets do NOT staple to bare executables** (stapling needs a container: .app/dmg/pkg), so "just notarize the helper" is not an option — the prototype must pick the artifact.

Evidence base today (plan, "Empirically verified"): npm-extracted binaries carry no quarantine xattr, ad-hoc signing suffices, no Gatekeeper prompt — **scoped to the npm path, n=1 machine, npm 10.9.3 extractor**. Carried unverified flags this ticket retires: "Notarization container for the helper → v0.3 D4 prototype"; "Quarantine test synthetic, npm extractor only → v0.3 install matrix". (CodeBurn's packaging/signing is also unverified — worth a look for competitive intel, not a gate.)

## What this gate decides and what it gates

- **The artifact**: (a) Developer-ID-signed **raw binary** — cannot be stapled, relies on Gatekeeper's *online* notarization check — vs (b) pulling the **flat `.app` bundle** forward from v0.5.
- **v0.5 brew cask**: a cask download IS quarantined; without notarization Gatekeeper blocks first launch — the cask plan is effectively gated on a GO.
- **Notifications/SMAppService timing**: they need the flat `.app`; the plan says v0.5 "or earlier if D4's notarization prototype forces it".
- **Confidence beyond npm**: whether pnpm/yarn/bun extractors and future macOS tightening can break first-launch on the status quo.

## Decision criteria (what must exist before the owner decides)

1. Build the candidate artifacts: ad-hoc-signed raw binary (status quo), Developer-ID-signed raw binary, and a signed + notarized + **stapled** flat `.app` (signed cells only possible after the owner funds the account — ad-hoc cells run first and never block on the decision).
2. Test each **online AND offline** — offline is where stapling matters; the offline-first-launch behavior of a signed-but-unstapled raw binary is the failure case to characterize precisely.
3. Exercise the **real extraction paths**: npm AND pnpm/yarn/bun, on **Intel + Apple Silicon clean VMs**, checking quarantine xattr presence and first-launch Gatekeeper behavior in every cell.
4. Record whether the ad-hoc status quo actually fails anywhere in that matrix. If it fails nowhere, NO-GO is cheap *now* — but the report must name the triggers that would reopen the decision (brew cask, notifications, macOS tightening).

## Consequences of each outcome

- **GO** ($99/yr paid, Developer ID obtained): pick the artifact from the prototype data. Signed raw binary → tarball layout unchanged but the offline-first-launch story must be documented and acceptable; flat `.app` pulled forward → packaging/CI changes land in v0.3–0.4 ahead of plan, and notifications/SMAppService unlock earlier. Brew cask in v0.5 becomes realistic.
- **NO-GO** (stay ad-hoc): npm-path extraction remains the **only** supported distribution channel; the install matrix must still widen the n=1 evidence to keep the claim honest; v0.5 brew cask is blocked or reduced to an npm-wrapping formula; the `.app`-dependent features stay v0.5+ with added risk; future macOS tightening of extraction-path handling becomes an accepted, unmitigated risk. Document all of this so v0.5 planning inherits it.

## Scope (out)

Actually shipping the chosen packaging (lands in v0.3/v0.5 per outcome); the brew cask itself (v0.5); wiring signing into release CI (follow-on after the decision).

## Constraints

Day-1 scheduling is deliberate: this ticket has no blockers in the tracker and must not wait behind T-014/T-015. Standing constraint interaction: the owner wants **no personal-name attribution** on the published package — note that a Developer ID certificate embeds the account holder's name, visible via `codesign -dv` on every shipped binary.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A written prototype report exists in the repo recording, for each matrix cell {ad-hoc raw, Developer-ID raw, notarized+stapled .app} × {online, offline} × {npm, pnpm, yarn, bun extraction} × {Intel, Apple Silicon clean VM}: quarantine xattr presence, Gatekeeper/spctl verdict, and observed first-launch behavior. Cells requiring the paid account are marked blocked-by-decision if NO-GO; all ad-hoc cells are complete regardless.
2. If GO: notarization submitted via notarytool; `stapler validate` passes on the .app; `codesign --verify --strict` passes on every signed artifact; `spctl --assess` output recorded per artifact.
3. The explicit decision is recorded (D4 marked DECIDED in the plan doc or ticket): go/no-go, chosen artifact, and rationale traceable to matrix cells.
4. Downstream consequences are written into the plan/roadmap per the outcome: brew-cask viability, whether the flat .app moves forward from v0.5, and (on NO-GO) the named triggers that reopen the decision.
5. The ticket started day-1 of v0.3 (not serialized behind T-014/T-015), or the deviation is explicitly justified in the report.

## Risks
Notarization without a paid Developer account is impossible — there is no free path; ad-hoc signing confers no Gatekeeper trust for quarantined files, so every non-npm distribution channel hangs on this decision. Apple account creation/approval latency can stall the day-1 gate (mitigation: run all ad-hoc cells first). The offline behavior of a signed-but-unstapled raw binary may be a dead end that forces the flat .app early, rippling into T-014 packaging and v0.4/v0.5 sequencing. The Developer ID certificate embeds a legal name, in tension with the standing no-personal-attribution constraint. Intel clean-VM testing has real hardware/licensing cost.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. The gate itself: does the owner fund the $99/yr Apple Developer membership and create the account? (Plan: 'Owner confirm pending'.)
2. If GO: personal vs organization Apple account — the signing certificate's subject name ships in every binary, and the owner has a standing no-personal-name-attribution rule for the npm package; does that rule extend to the code-signing identity?
3. Budget/approval for Intel + Apple Silicon clean-VM infrastructure for the extraction matrix.
title: D4 go/no-go: signing + notarization artifact prototype
